messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sustained surge detected on /v1/generate and fallbacks. onset ~2212345500. Paging primary oncall. dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.internal/alerts/2212
Maya R: taking the page, joining. quick status?
Support-Bot: multiple enterprise customers reporting latency and 429s (org-13, org-72). Escalation noted at 2212345524.
Jin K: quick summary: overall p95 for text-gen jumped to 1.1s, error fraction rose to ~2.9% in last 6m. dedicated-us-west-1 and dedicated-eu-2 show high queue depths. Autoscaler logs show repeated "scale_up_failed: reached_max_instances" for eu-2. Burst capacity is disabled per policy.
Maya R: probable cause: sudden traffic spike + new LLP logits_filtering flag increasing per-token CPU. Mitigations to consider: enable burst for impacted Dedicated pools, temporarily raise autoscale caps, apply soft global throttles for non-critical routes, and disable the experimental flag.
Oliver P: Agreed. Prioritize gen traffic for earlier slots. I'll prepare a soft token-based rate limit for embedding and rerank routes and patch routing weights to route background jobs to smaller models.
Sara N: I'll request emergency approval for burst enabling and document the justification. This will be flagged in the postmortem.
Maya R: executing burst toggle + emergency cap bump now. Command:
```
# emergency: enable burst and raise cap
redwoodctl pool update --name dedicated-eu-2 --burst-enabled true --burst-size 8
redwoodctl autoscale set --pool dedicated-eu-2 --max-instances 36 --min-instances 6
```
Maya R: API accepted 202, starting rollout at 2212345600.
Evan (SRE): applying traffic shaping rule for low-priority routes: `route:/v1/embeddings -> quota 12r/s/org (soft)` and `route:/v1/rerank -> quota 8r/s/org`. This should free GPU capacity for generation.
Jin K: reverting the logits_filtering experimental flag now — it's causing extra compute. Running: `featurectl rollback logits_filtering --scope dedicated`
Jin K: flag rollback completed at 2212345695.
Maya R: telemetry: dedicated-eu-2 queue 590 -> 280 in 3m. p95 down from 1.1s to 480ms. error fraction 2.9% -> 0.9%.
Support-Bot: customer update: org-72 still saw intermittent 429s but frequency dropped significantly; support notified.
Oliver P: good. Note: monitor burst instance health and KV cache warmup. If cache misses persist, latency may re-spike.
Evan (SRE): extra instances are provisioning; autoscaler logs now show successful scale events. KV warming in progress — hit rates improving. No measurables of increased OOMs.
Maya R: on-call handoff: I'll brief the relief in 20m. Changes to communicate: burst=true on eu-2, max-instances=36, logits_filtering disabled, soft throttles on embeddings/rerank. All changes tagged as emergency and temporary.
Sara N: ticketing: recording all mitigation commands in incident tracker and adding a follow-up action to run a capacity planning/traffic-shaping playbook for Dedicated during large tenant bursts.
Jin K: reminder: we'll want a config to auto-enable burst when queue depth > 400 and autoscaler reports "reached_max_instances" to avoid manual toggles. Add to RFC backlog.
Maya R: final check at 2212345920: p95 stable at 260ms, error fraction 0.15%, queue depth ~45. Switching incident state to monitoring. Leaving presence for next 30m for regression watch.
IncidentBot: Status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. If regressions occur, re-ping with `@eng-oncall` and reopen. :white_check_mark:
